_what_this_is: The committed measurement record behind README.md's Performance table (ADR-0042 D7). Every absolute figure published there is bound to an entry here, and PerformanceTableCoherenceTests fails the build when the two disagree. This file is the record; README.md is the claim. When they differ, the claim moves — unless a re-measurement says otherwise, in which case this file moves in its own reviewed commit.
_this_is_not_the_regression_gate: Correspondence between document and record is this file's job. Regression protection is Tests/Verbara.Sdk.Benchmarks/baseline.json, which holds HOSTED-RUNNER means and is a different measurement on different hardware. The two are separate failures and are detected separately (ADR-0042 D4 vs D7).

measurement.note: The AMI row is the one exception to the header above: its post-patch figure was taken on .NET 10.0.6 with MediumRunJob (30 samples), recorded in benchmark-analysis.md section 1.1. Stated per row rather than hidden behind a single header.

rows.note: README published 653 ns / 1.53M until this change. That is the PRE-patch ShortRun figure from :105; the patch recovered ~35 ns and the record's own 'Throughput final' line says 1.62M. The published claim understated the SDK.
The benchmark method is named LookupByUniqueId; the README names the public API. Both are correct for their audience, but a reader diffing the two will not find a match.
Derived: 20.7 ns for 100 observers. docs/README-technical.md publishes 22.8 ns for the same measurement, which matches no committed value — that block is being replaced with the v1.11 figures.

Fact+Stopwatch against local Docker, not BenchmarkDotNet — the table header above does not describe this row's instrument. docs/guides/session-store-backends.md:179 publishes ~250 µs for the same measurement and is wrong.

deferred_rows.why_not_bound: The record measures code that no longer ships. benchmark-analysis.md:149 describes the store as 'Npgsql + Dapper + JSONB', and :157 attributes the batch figure to 'Dapper no tiene COPY'. Dapper was removed repo-wide in v2.2.0 under ADR-0022 Phase D. Binding this row would pin a public claim to a measurement of deleted code.
deferred_rows.unblocking_condition: Re-measure Verbara.Sdk.Sessions.Postgres on the current NpgsqlExecutor path (Testcontainers, postgres:18-alpine), commit the result here, then bind. Until then the figure stays published and unguarded, which is stated rather than hidden.
deferred_rows.also_note: docs/guides/session-store-backends.md:9-11 publishes Postgres read latency as 5-10 ms where the record has GetAsync p50 = 51 µs. That divergence is separate from the Dapper problem and outlives it.
